Subject: Aurora Labs — Dedicated capacity orchestration & onboarding pulse

Hi Lina / Rajiv —

Thanks again for the conversation last week. We're kicking off the dedicated capacity onboarding for Aurora Labs and want to align a high-level orchestration plan so engineering and procurement can move in parallel. Key items we need from you to finalize the activation schedule and regional choices: 

1) Expected steady-state concurrent requests (p50/p95 latency targets) and peak daily token throughput — this will let us size the GPU pool and choose an initial instance mix.
2) Preferred primary region(s) for serving and any regulatory constraints (e.g., all EU-only datasets).
3) KMS / key custody preference and whether you require HSM-backed keys for model inputs.
4) Are there expected weekly burst windows (cron data processing, CI tests) that will require burst capacity above baseline? If so, specify magnitude and duration.

Our proposed sequencing (tentative):
- Requirements freeze and MOP (mutual action plan) by 2026-12-03
- Pool provisioning and network handoff (VPC peering / routing) 2026-12-06—2026-12-10
- Canary / perf validation with sample prompts 2026-12-11—2026-12-16
- Go-live window targeted 2026-12-20 (subject to pass signal)

On the ops side, Monica will handle runbook and CS checks, Karthik will manage provisioning milestones, and Soojin will validate autoscale/burst policies with the infra team. I'll coordinate client-facing approvals and the SLA discussion.

Please reply with the requested items and attach any internal capacity documents. If procurement needs a separate thread for SOW/redlines, copy procurement@auroralabs.com and we'll route accordingly.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this running.

Best,
Markus Klein
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Aurora Labs — Dedicated capacity orchestration & onboarding pulse

Hi Markus —

Appreciate the clear sequencing. Quick answers inline: 

1) Throughput/traffic: steady-state target is ~120 concurrent inference sessions (p50 target 120ms, p95 300ms) with expected steady token throughput ~120M tokens/day. Peak bursts can reach ~300M tokens/day during nightly batch runs (01:00–03:00 PT), typically 2–3 days/week.

2) Region: primary preference is us-west1 for latency and proximity to our main infra; EU fallback is required for certain customers but won't be the default. Data residency: production PII will live in us-west1; non-PII analytics can replicate.

3) KMS: we require customer-managed keys (we use AWS KMS with HSM class). We'll share KMS ARNs and an onboarding checklist with our security team.

4) Burst windows: see (1) — nightly batch jobs and an internal QA stress test every Friday 02:00–04:00 PT that may require +2x baseline for up to 2 hours.

Attached: aurora_capacity_requirements_v1.pdf (includes usage curves and sample prompt sizes). Procurement copied for SOW coordination.

Thanks,
Lina Park
Head of Product Ops — Aurora Labs
lina@auroralabs.com

Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Aurora Labs — Dedicated capacity orchestration & onboarding pulse

Thanks Lina — that usage profile is very helpful. Quick operational notes and proposed defaults so we can lock the MOP: 

- Pool sizing: propose an initial pool of 8 x A100-80GB-equivalent nodes with mixed model placement (2 nodes pinned for synchronous low-latency endpoints, 6 nodes as shared workers for batch/async). This targets your p95 goals with ~25% headroom for short bursts.

- Autoscale & burst policy (proposed): baseline auto-scaling set to maintain p50 latency targets using continuous batching; scale-up threshold at 75% avg GPU utilization over a 5-minute window; emergency burst policy allows temporary 2.5x capacity for up to 3 hours (requires explicit billing pre-approval). We will bake in manual approvals to cover your Friday QA runs automatically once procurement approves the burst SOW.

- Regional failover: primary us-west1 with automated fallback to eu-west1 for specific customers. We recommend async replication for non-PII and active-active only after additional compliance signoff; otherwise we operate active-primary with cold-standby to avoid cross-border PII copies.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Aurora: finalize KMS ARNs + confirm procurement SOW acceptance (Aurora / procurement) — ETA 2026-12-03.
- Redwood: create runbook (monica) + provision network VLANs and peering (karthik) — ETA request 2026-12-06.
- Redwood Infra: pre-provision burst capacity quota and reserve (soojin) — ETA 2026-12-05.

I'll attach a mutual action plan spreadsheet and a short checklist for the runbook. Once procurement confirms SOW, we can exec the provisioning window.

Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai

Team —

Great progress. Per Monica's plan and Lina's answers, I'm summarizing the mutual action plan and next steps so everyone has a single source of truth: 

1) Procurement / SOW: Aurora procurement to sign off on the burst SOW that authorizes 2.5x temporary capacity and the associated billing terms. Procurement indicated they'll review by EOD 2026-12-03 (procurement@auroralabs.com).

2) Security / KMS: Aurora to share KMS ARNs and the principal we'll use to grant decrypt permissions. We'll coordinate a short audit of key usage with our security team.

3) Networking / VPC: Karthik will send the VPC peering template and the required CIDR ranges. Expect a request for a test peer by 2026-12-05.

4) Provisioning / Canary: Assuming SOW and KMS are in place, we will reserve the initial pool (8 GPUs) and run canary traffic 2026-12-11—12-16. Soojin will pre-book burst quota for Friday tests.

5) Acceptance & Go-live: target 2026-12-20 for production cutover pending canary pass.

Links and tickets: onboarding runbook (https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2bRWI-aurora-onboard), provisioning ticket INF-2987 (https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INF-2987), HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deal/54321.

Please reply with any redlines or constraints; if procurement requires a separate SOW thread, confirm and we'll open a dedicated email for finance/legal. Otherwise, Monica and Karthik will begin the provisioning checklist and Jonas will coordinate the perf tests.

Thanks all — excited to get this moving.

—
